name: Periodic OPSEC review and adaptation
description: The adversary treats operational security as a continuously evolving practice requiring scheduled review: rotation of cryptographic keys, regular updates to security-critical software, periodic review of identity and infrastructure for lingering exposure, and willingness to abandon compromised or outdated identities. Attachment to familiar tools or long-lived identities is a documented failure mode.

subtechniques.name: Scheduled cryptographic key rotation
subtechniques.description: The adversary rotates PGP keys, session keys, and other long-lived cryptographic credentials on a defined schedule. Long-lived keys accumulate risk: more ciphertext for cryptanalysis, possible undetected exposure, and a long attribution history linked to a single fingerprint.
